item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I laughed quite heartily at "it's supposed to do that, never mind."

This very much feels like the American counterpart to SCP-1150-J.

I don't care if it's an old joke, it was funny, and I choose to believe that it actually is anomalous in a really boring way.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
We shouldn't even have a concept of a budget, we're the Foundation for christ's sake; we spend billions of dollars for some overly-fancy storage locker with a bunch of dumbass redundancies

This part is admittedly funny. It could be -J concept on its own. But it's only a shoutout here.

Really? This article got through to the system? Who the fuck maintains our database, lobotomized monkeys? God, I swear, it's like no one else works here. I hate this place.

Frankly, this is a bit too meta for me and is awkward as a punchline for me…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The addendum is what sold it for me. Sure, he accidentally hit "submit" - and then someone approved the file for publication as an official document. "Who maintains our database, lobotomized monkeys?"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This time it made me laugh.
The downplayed snark here really sells it for me as something this guy hammered out while angrily eating a scorched, half frozen burrito and accidentally hit "submit to database"

edit: I think what I love so much here is that it plays into the daily life side of the Foundation, which we don't see too often. I have to imagine that once you get past that initial gee-whiz of working for a secret organization protecting the universe from cosmic threats, yadda yadda yadda, you start to run into the same burnout as with any other job. For your typical site staff, most days probably involve more paperwork, lukewarm casserole, and endless repetition of containment procedures than containment breaches and facinating experimentation with eldritch artifacts.

item.content:encoded: Well, I mean… technically it's Safe, and the rest of the article is joke-y enough to the point that I'd think using an 'accurate' Object Class wouldn't detract from the humor. Then again, you could always go for the OTT "ERMERGHERD KETER KILL IT" or whatever; although I've never really preferred that in -Js, I know some people do. Really it's up to you, and I do suppose "should be Neutralized" would go along with the rest of the humor style.

item.title: (no title)

The concept, while chuckle-worthy on its own, gets old fast and the diction isn't the type of hyperbole that makes me laugh. That combined with the frequent first-person in the Description killed it for me.

Object Class: Thaumiel, because the Site Director's too goddamn cheap to buy a new one.

Also, I don't understand this part. Thaumiel is the class that 'is the box' (contains other anomalies) so I don't see how that has anything to do with the Site Director refusing to replace it.
